answer:
Given that your mole has changed color significantly and sometimes bleeds, you should see a doctor as soon as possible. These changes can be signs of something serious, such as skin cancer (including melanoma), and it’s important to get it evaluated promptly.

What you should do:

Schedule an appointment with a dermatologist or your primary care doctor as soon as possible.
If the mole starts bleeding heavily, becomes very painful, or you feel unwell, seek urgent medical attention.
In the meantime:
Try not to pick at or irritate the mole.
Keep the area clean and covered if it’s bleeding.
Note any other changes (size, shape, texture, itching, pain) so you can report them accurately.
Protect the area from sun exposure.

Early evaluation makes a big difference, so please don’t wait to get it checked.
